pdf§pages§0§p§0: The ceramics and tableware market in France — a summary prepared for the “Spring launch” project.
pdf§pages§0§p§1: Written by Camille Laurent with support from Studio Nord. Figures as of June 30, 2026.
pdf§pages§1§p§0: The tableware market grew 6.8% year over year, driven by direct sales and independent shops.
pdf§pages§1§p§1: The average gross margin of workshops reached 41%, up two points thanks to lower energy costs.
pdf§pages§1§p§2: Customers aged 25 to 40 now account for 38% of online purchases.
pdf§pages§2§p§0: Segment revenue reached €1.6 billion in the second quarter, 6.8% growth over Q2 2025.
pdf§pages§2§p§1: Online sales make up 27% of the total, up from 21% two years ago. Trade fairs remain the top acquisition channel for 61% of workshops.
pdf§pages§3§p§0: Three players dominate distribution: two shop networks and one specialist marketplace.
pdf§pages§3§p§1: Atelier Morel stands out with a margin 6 points above average, thanks to small-batch production.
pdf§pages§4§p§0: The average basket is €86, up 9%. Gifts account for 44% of the quarter’s sales.
pdf§pages§4§p§1: Loyalty is rising: 31% of customers buy at least twice a year.
pdf§pages§5§p§0: List prices rose 3.2% on average, with no visible effect on volumes.
pdf§pages§5§p§1: Gross margin remains under pressure on glazed pieces, whose firing cost has doubled since 2023.
pdf§pages§6§p§0: Independent shops remain the top channel, ahead of online sales and trade fairs.
pdf§pages§6§p§1: Online sales grow mostly in the evening and on weekends; 64% are placed on mobile.
pdf§pages§7§p§0: Spring accounts for 28% of annual sales, just behind the holiday season.
pdf§pages§7§p§1: A late-March launch catches Mother’s Day and wedding registries.
pdf§pages§8§p§0: Raw material costs may rise in the second half.
pdf§pages§8§p§1: Kiln delivery times: up to 14 weeks at the main manufacturers.
pdf§pages§9§p§0: Launch the collection in late March, with an early preview for loyal customers.
pdf§pages§9§p§1: Protect the margin by keeping glazed items to 30% of the range.
pdf§pages§10§p§0: Online survey of 1,240 customers and interviews with 22 workshops, June 2 to 26, 2026.
pdf§pages§10§p§1: Market figures come from the French crafts observatory and the national statistics office.
pdf§pages§11§p§0: Detailed tables by region, the full questionnaire and the list of workshops interviewed.
pdf§pages§11§p§1: Contact: Camille Laurent, project lead, camille.laurent@studionord.fr.

pdf§ask§sugg§1: What is the average gross margin?
pdf§ask§sugg§2: What are the risks for the launch?

pdf§ask§answers§0§a: The average gross margin of workshops is 41% (page 2), up two points. Atelier Morel does 6 points better (page 4).
pdf§ask§answers§1§a: Two main risks (page 9): higher material costs in the second half and kiln delivery times of up to 14 weeks.
pdf§ask§fallback: In short: market up 6.8%, 41% margin, online sales at 27%, spring = 28% of annual sales. Recommendation: launch in late March (page 10).
pdf§summary§1§b:
Here’s the gist of the 12 pages:
1. The market grew 6.8% year over year (p. 3).
2. The average gross margin is 41% (p. 2).
3. Online sales are 27% of sales, 64% of them on mobile (p. 7).
4. Spring accounts for 28% of annual sales (p. 8).
5. Recommendation: launch in late March and keep glazed items to 30% of the range (p. 10).
pdf§act§explain: Gross margin is revenue minus the cost of the pieces sold (clay, glaze, firing). At 41%, a bowl sold for €30 leaves €12.30 to pay for the workshop, rent and salaries.
pdf§act§summarize: Workshops keep 41 cents of gross margin per euro sold on average, two points better than in 2025.
pdf§act§quote: “The average gross margin of workshops reached 41%, up two points.” — Q2 2026 market study, p. 2.

audio§segs§0§text: Hi everyone, thanks for coming. Let’s review the spring launch: timeline, booth and budget.
audio§segs§1§text: On the workshop side, the 120 pieces of the “Lagon” collection will be ready on April 2, glazing included.
audio§segs§2§text: Studio Nord sent us the booth quote: €9,800 excl. tax, setup included. That’s €600 over budget.
audio§segs§3§text: We can make up for it by dropping the extra lighting. Julien, are you OK with that?
audio§segs§4§text: Yes, the hall lighting is enough if we keep the light oak shelves.
audio§segs§5§text: For communication, I suggest three posts a week from March 24, with Camille’s photos.
audio§segs§6§text: Decision: launch on April 14, booth approved without lighting, Inès runs the posting schedule.
audio§segs§7§text: I’ll send the shop window visuals by Friday.
audio§segs§8§text: Next check-in March 21 at 10 AM, same room.
